Today it was all about PCB things – week 1 design, PCB week. Spent almost all day working in KiCad doing the schematic for ShadowComms: ESP32-WROOM-32E, SX1262 LoRa via SPI header, TP4056 charger, USB-C port, e-ink FPC connector, piezo buzzer, two buttons (SW).

The most challenging part of this work was dealing with symbol libraries – had to create all the symbols inside the .kicad_sch file (lib_symbols) to avoid using additional libraries in the future. Very frustrating experience because of manually drawn pin shapes and writing the names.

In the very end, during the attempt to push changes to GitHub, I've got a problem with kicad-cli error (Failed to load schematic). Surprised me and made me waste another hour. CLI works absolutely fine with E:/KiCad/share/kicad/demos/ecc83/ecc83-pp_v2.kicad_sch, while my schema E:/shadowcomms_pcb/shadowcomms.kicad_sch fails constantly. Tried a lot of things: replace UUIDs with regular expression, move files to other directories... Even v2_demo file fails on E drive. Now I am pretty sure that it is a disk mounting problem of E: drive, the Windows mount prevent
s the CLI from loading files. Right now my main schema is working fine.

yo short update for week 1 pcb / hardware prep. finally finished mapping out all connections for shadowcomms and made the bom table so i can order parts without forgetting something stupid.

spent hours staring at pinouts coz esp32 pin management is a nightmare fr. got the sx1262 lora module hooked over spi (sck, mosi, miso, cs, rst, busy etc), plus the 2.9" e-paper display shares the spi bus with its own cs/dc/rst pins. for power system using tp4056 charge controller + boost converter to step up battery voltage for the components. keyboard is connected via gpio expander (tca9555) to save esp32 pins coz i ran out of io fast lol.

also made a full schematic block diagram and breadboard wiring layout in wokwi / easyeda just to be 100% sure I didnt cross any traces or short power to gnd.

bom list came out to like ~$64 total which is not bad considering e-ink displays are pricey. ordering main mcu (esp32-wroom-32e) from mouser, lora module & buttons from ali/lcsc, and getting custom 2-layer pcb printed at jlcpcb.
